w10_P4_000628: A depot report ends with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 14 kN off a figure that is 4 times a converted reading, since 4 tugs work the yard. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a load of 133000 grams. The load's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 393 and 49 exactly, with nothing left over. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000633: A teaching bench launches a puck of 3000 grams across a smooth surface. The puck's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. The bench records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. It adds a standing instrument allowance of 9 kJ, subtracts a contractual credit of 22 kJ, and multiplies what remains by 10 because 10 benches report together. The bench is 1.3 m wide, a dimension never used in the calculation. What number, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000638: A crash-test facility launches a trolley of 40000 grams along a straight track. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is 5 times the sum of 3 and 10. The logger records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 6 for the 6 trolleys in a run, and then by 4 for the 4 runs in the programme. The track is 90 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?
w10_P4_000640: A laboratory record ends with a value found by adding a fixed instrument offset of 17 J to the energy a carrier of 23 kg holds because of its motion. The carrier's launch speed in metres per second is built up as follows: take the value that the rate curve 1t^2 + 3t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second starting from zero, with t the time in seconds, multiply it by 2 for the twin drive, and multiply the result by 5 for the five-stage booster. The launch rail is 7 m long, a dimension the record never uses. What value, in joules, ends the record?
w10_P4_000641: A test bench launches a slider of 4000 grams along a level rail. A base value in metres per second is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 0t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds, and adding a drive contribution of 17 to that base value gives the slider's launch speed. The bench records the energy the slider carries because of its motion and expresses the record in kilojoules. That converted figure is multiplied by 6, because 6 benches report together. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000643: A calibration rig holds 6 identical reference masses, and the acceleration it applies, in metres per second squared, is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from them. That acceleration is given to a shuttle of 57000 grams. From the force needed to drive the shuttle the controller subtracts a frame tare of 1 N, then multiplies the remainder by 3 because the routine runs on 3 axes, and expresses the result in kilonewtons. The rig bed is 2 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000644: A workshop ledger closes with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 26 kN off a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 6 times the force needed to drive one carrier, since 6 carriers run together. Each carrier has a mass of 10000 grams, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is 3 times the sum of 3 and 6, with a drive contribution of 30 added to that product. The workshop floor is 15 m long, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000648: A plant drives a carrier of 193 kg along its line, and the carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared is 2 times the sum of 8 and 8. The controller records the force needed to drive one carrier and multiplies it by 6 for the 6 carriers on a line, by 3 for the 3 lines in a bay, by 11 for the 11 bays in the plant, and by 8 for the 8 plants in the group. The bay roof stands 9 m above the floor, a height the controller never uses. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000652: A workshop counts 208 washers in one tray and 248 in another, and the technician works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. Subtracting a slip loss of 3 from that number gives, in metres per second, the launch speed of a carrier of 49000 grams. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and subtracts a friction allowance of 15 J, then expresses the remainder in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 4, because 4 benches report together. The bench is 1.5 m wide, a dimension never used here. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000654: A laboratory figure is 2 times a paired total, since the runs are paired, and that paired total is itself 2 times a bench value because two benches contribute. The bench value is what remains after a friction allowance of 11 J is taken from a reading that was itself a fixed instrument offset of 17 J added to the energy a carrier of 49000 grams holds because of its motion. The carrier's launch speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 315 and 65 exactly, with nothing left over. What is the laboratory figure, in joules?
w10_P4_000659: A plant ledger closes with a number that is 12 N more than a figure, and that figure was itself 28 N more than a line total. The line total is 11 times a bay figure, and the bay figure is 12 times the force needed to accelerate one carrier of 191000 grams. The carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 122 and 51 exactly, with nothing left over. The plant floor is 40 m long, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in newtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000663: A laboratory total is 10 times a site figure, because 10 sites run the same rig, and each site figure is 9 times a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a value that is 2 times the energy of a single release, since 2 releases make a pair. In one release a glider of 36 kg slides along the track, and its release speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 338 and 24 exactly, with nothing left over. The track is 2 m long, a dimension never used here. What is the laboratory total, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000666: A gantry drives a carriage of 101000 grams along its beam, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 8 times the sum of 4 and 2. The controller works out the force needed to drive the carriage and expresses it in kilonewtons. That converted figure is multiplied by 6 for the 6 carriages on the beam, a fixed frame allowance of 23 kN is added, and the result is multiplied by 2 because the hall has two identical gantries. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000676: A test report ends with a value in kilojoules, converted from a figure obtained by adding a fixed instrument offset of 22 J to a run total. The run total is 9 times the energy of a single launch, since 9 launches make a run. In one launch a carrier of 15 kg leaves the rail, and its launch speed in metres per second is 3 times the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. The launch rail is 9 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000677: A gantry drives a carriage of 160000 grams along its beam, and the carriage's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 4x^3 - 4x^2, with x the time in seconds. The acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which that fitted position curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second. The controller works out the force needed to drive the carriage, multiplies it by 11 because 11 carriages run together, and expresses the total in kilonewtons. It then adds a fixed frame allowance of 23 kN and subtracts a handling credit of 7 kN. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000682: A stores clerk counts 192 bolts of one type and 113 of another, and works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A slider of 4000 grams is launched along the bench at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the slider holds because of its motion, adds a fixed instrument offset of 10 J, and expresses the result in kilojoules. A contractual credit of 25 kJ is then subtracted, and what remains is multiplied by 5 because 5 benches report together. The bench is 1.8 m long, a dimension never used in the calculation. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000686: A warehouse tug accelerates a pallet of 83 kg across a smooth floor. The pallet's acceleration in metres per second squared is found by taking the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0 and adding a drive contribution of 8 to it. The controller works out the force needed for the pull and multiplies it by 3, because the shift calls for 3 identical pulls. The total is then expressed in kilonewtons. The pallet is stacked 2 m high, a figure the controller never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000696: A launch bench brings a slider of 2000 grams up to speed, and the slider's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 7t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 1 second and t = 2 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the slider carries because of its motion, subtracts a friction allowance of 3 J, and expresses the remainder in kilojoules. From the converted figure a contractual credit of 29 kJ is subtracted, and a further handling credit of 28 kJ is subtracted after that. The bench is 1.1 m wide, a dimension never used here. What number, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000699: A laboratory report ends with a value in kilojoules, converted from a figure that is 11 times a run total, and each run total is 6 times the energy of a single launch. In one launch a carrier of 15000 grams leaves the rail, and the energy of the launch is the energy the carrier holds because of its motion. Its launch speed in metres per second is found by taking the largest whole number that divides both 166 and 345 exactly with nothing left over, and adding a drive contribution of 20 to it. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000700: A launch bench brings a carriage of 55000 grams up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 3t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. A standing instrument allowance of 17 kJ is added, and the sum is multiplied by 12 because 12 benches report together. The rail is 30 m long, a length the bench never uses. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000701: A laboratory total is found by taking a calibration credit of 26 kJ off a figure that is 8 times a converted reading, since 8 benches contribute. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a value that is 3 times the energy of one release, because 3 releases make a set. In each release a carrier of 32 kg moves at a speed, in metres per second, given by the rate at which the slope of the fitted position curve 4x^3 - 6x^2 is itself changing at the instant x = 3 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. What is the laboratory total, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000706: A conveyor test launches a carton of 16000 grams along the rollers. The carton's launch speed in metres per second is found by taking 5 times the sum of 5 and 3 and then subtracting a slip loss of 25 from the result. The bench records the energy the carton carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 6, because 6 cartons go out in a batch. A fixed instrument offset of 6 J is added to the batch total. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000716: A launcher brings a sled of 42 kg up to speed along a level track. A base value in metres per second is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds starting from zero, with t the time in seconds, and adding a drive contribution of 30 to that base gives the sled's speed. The logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion, subtracts a friction allowance of 18 J, and expresses the remainder in kilojoules. The track is 100 m long, a length the logger never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the logger report?
w10_P4_000729: A test rig launches a carrier of 49000 grams along its rail. The carrier's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 1x^3 + 6x^2, with x the time in seconds, and the rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives a base value. Adding a drive contribution of 22 to that base, and then a further booster contribution of 18, gives the launch speed in metres per second. The rig records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and multiplies it by 9 for the 9 launches in a run, and by 6 for the 6 runs in the programme. What total, in joules, does the rig report?
w10_P4_000731: A crash-test facility launches a trolley of 47000 grams, and its launch speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 7 and 13. The logger records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 trolleys go out in a run. The run total is expressed in kilojoules, a standing instrument allowance of 26 kJ is added, and the result is multiplied by 10 for the 10 runs in the programme. The track is 75 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?
